name: False Dichotomy
shortDef: Presenting two options as the only ones when others exist.
definition: Framing a choice as if only two options exist, often one of them obviously bad, when there are other reasonable alternatives or ways to combine the options.
howToSpot: Can you name a third option, or a mix of the two?
Watch for "either... or" framing that isn't backed up.
Could both options be true, or both false, at the same time?
classicExample: Either we cancel the school play or we accept that the whole arts budget will collapse.
legitimateVersion: Some choices really are binary, like a yes-or-no decision or a road that forks two ways. Narrowing to two is fair once you've shown the others don't work.

contrast.fal_middle_ground: A false dichotomy hides the middle options; the middle ground fallacy assumes the middle option must be the right one.
contrast.fal_loaded_question: A false dichotomy offers too few options; a loaded question smuggles a disputed assumption into the question itself.
